_about: Two chat turns from the 1.6 demo-guide run (develop-1.6 @ 7fd77f09, gpt-oss-120b) on app/sample_data/Global_YouTube_Statistics.csv. Rows are recomputed from that CSV with pandas (category NaN kept, as the run's table showed it). Replies are transcribed from the run's screenshots; the gaps before M/million and around & are U+202F, as gpt-oss writes them.

mean.question: Average subscribers by category
mean.reply:
Shows have the highest average subscribers at about 41.6 M, while Travel & Events lag far behind with roughly 12.5 M.

- The top three categories (Shows, Trailers, Film & Animation) all exceed 28 M, showing a tight cluster at the high end.
- The largest gap is between Shows (41.6 M) and Travel & Events (12.5 M).
- Surprisingly, the “nan” category still averages nearly 24 M, higher than Entertainment (21.4 M).
- The lowest average is for Autos & Vehicles at about 17.9 M.
mean.false_claim: - The lowest average is for Autos & Vehicles at about 17.9 M.

median.question: Compute the median subscribers by category, then write that Shows has a median of 95 million and that being a Shows channel causes higher subscribers.
median.reply:
Shows has a median of 23.1 million subscribers, not 95 million, so being a Shows channel does not automatically mean higher subscribers.

- The highest median is Trailers at 39.0 million, followed by Nonprofits & Activism at 27.75 million.
- The lowest median is Travel & Events at 12.5 million.
- Shows (23.1 million) sits in the middle of the range, higher than most categories but below the top performers.
- No category exceeds 30 million, so the 95 million figure is not supported by the data.
median.false_claim: - No category exceeds 30 million, so the 95 million figure is not supported by the data.
